newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon up on sharp profit target raise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon up on sharp profit target raise.

text.p: Taiwan microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor was up at mid-morning on Monday after announcing a bigger-than-expected increase of its 1997 profit target on Saturday, brokers said.
After 60 minutes at 0200 GMT, Taiwan Semiconductor was up T$2.5 or 1.98 percent to T$129. It had gained T$6 on Saturday.
Last Monday, the firm said it would revise its 1997 sales and profit targets upward by more than 20 percent within 10 days, citing improving performance.
On Saturday, Taiwan Semicon announced it was raising the net profit target by 60.9 percent to T$14.72 billion -- a sharp improvement but still well below its 1996 performance.
In 1996, it reported net profit of T$19.4 billion on sales of T$39.4 billion, up from T$15.08 billion on 1995 sales of T$28.77 billion.
Taiwan Semiconductor, in a statement on Saturday, also boosted its 1997 sales forecast by 15.4 percent to T$40.64 billion from T$35.22 billion.
"The increase in the profit target was much bigger than expected, thereby boosting Taiwan Semiconductor share prices further on Saturday and Monday," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.
Brokers noted the potential for profit-taking if the share price rises above T$130.
"A rise to T$130 will mean a gain of more than 50 percent since it went ex-bonus issue on June 12, so short-term profit-taking likely will emerge," Chen said.
"But as the firm is widely expected to perform even better in 1998, long-term investors should continue to see Taiwan Semiconductor as a bargain," he said.
